catalog_quote: [Lastra 1986, c. p. 21:] El acento se marca cuando no recae en la penúltima sílaba o en monosílabos. [c. p. 232, Sur de Guerrero = Cuautepec (Gro. 12), Santa María Acatepec, Ometepec (Gro. 13), Quetzalapa, Azoyú (Gro. 14), Macahuite y Zoyatlán (Gro. 15):] ... fonología de Cuautepec es bastante peculiar. Lo más saliente es: /g/ inicial e intervocálica: giabít 'lluvia' (20), teguli? 'carbón' (6) ... /b/ donde otros dialectos tienen /w/: giabít 'lluvia' (20); /w/ para /k"/: witapán 'detrás' (401). Además es frecuente el acento final. Este dialecto amerita sin duda más análisis y más estudio. En cuanto a los otros tres puntos del Sur de Guerrero, Gro. 15 es más 'central' porque tiene // aunque no final en monosílabos: al 'agua' (1), tel 'piedra' (396), pero por lo general se asemeja mucho a Gro. 13 y 14. ... (Véase Valiñas, 1981) Podemos decir que estos tres puntos son bastante periféricos …

new_statements.translation: [Conventions:] Stress is marked when it does not fall on the penultimate syllable, or on monosyllables. [p. 232:] ... the phonology of Cuautepec is quite peculiar. Most salient: initial and intervocalic /g/ ..., /b/ where other dialects have /w/ ..., /w/ for /kʷ/: witapán 'behind'. In addition, final stress is frequent. This dialect certainly deserves more analysis and study. As for the other three points of Southern Guerrero [Acatepec-Ometepec, Quetzalapa-Azoyú, Zoyatlán], Gro. 15 is more 'central' because it has /tl/ ... but in general it closely resembles Gro. 13 and 14. ... (See Valiñas 1981.) We can say these three points are fairly peripheral

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lastra transcribes Nahuatl with penultimate stress as the unmarked default and marks only deviations; for her 'Sur de Guerrero' subarea she states that word-final stress is frequent at Cuautepec (Gro. 12; her cited forms giabít, witapán are final-stressed), while for the nht core points Santa Cruz Acatepec (Ometepec) and Quetzalapa (Azoyú) she makes no stress remark, leaving them in the default penultimate transcription. No source read states a stress rule for Ometepec Nahuatl proper.
new_statements.exceptions: Cuautepec (Gro. 12): 'es frecuente el acento final' -- a tendency, not a rule, with no conditioning given; Lastra flags the dialect as needing more study. Ethnologue does not list Cuautepec among nht localities, though Canger 1986 and Lastra 1986 group Cuau(h)tepec with Azoyú and Ometepec as the southern/coastal dialect.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms from Lastra's dialect questionnaire (numbered items, e.g. 20 'lluvia', 401 'detrás'); read only through Google Books snippets, so the full paragraph and any further prosodic remarks on pp. 231-233 were not seen.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog omet1237 = Ethnologue nht (Acatepec, Arcelia, El Carmen, Quetzalapa de Azoyú, Rancho de Cuananchinicha in Guerrero; Cruz Alta, San Vicente Piñas, Concepción Guerrero in Oaxaca; 'may be 3 separate languages'). Lastra 1986's 'Sur de Guerrero' subarea and Canger 1986's 'náhuatl del Sur / de la Costa de Guerrero' cover Cuau(h)tepec + Azoyú + Ometepec; the one explicit stress remark found ('frecuente el acento final') concerns Cuautepec (Lastra's Gro. 12), a markedly divergent point that Ethnologue does not list under nht and that has no glottocode of its own; the nht core points (Santa Cruz Acatepec, Ometepec = Gro. 13; Quetzalapa, Azoyú = Gro. 14) receive no stress remark. INALI's 2008 catalogue registers no Nahuatl variant for these Costa Chica municipalities at all.

sources.note: Defines 'náhuatl del Sur o de la costa de Guerrero (municipios de Cuauhtepec, Azoyú y Ometepec)' (p. 281), based on Valiñas's questionnaires for Lastra plus her own unpublished 1976 Quetzalapa notes (p. 284); lists six morphological/lexical traits and 'una diferencia bastante profunda entre el dialecto de Cuauhtepec y los de Azoyú y Ometepec' (p. 285).
